title: Window Hopper - Supports selecting window with the mouse
author: hjtgh
summary: Window Hopper already renders selectable tiles but its native overlay handles no mouse activation messages, making pointer selection a bounded interaction design.

status.label: Design investigation queued
status.detail: The request is narrow and current code exposes tile geometry, selection, and commit functions that can support a concrete design without more reporter evidence.

judgment.rationale: The request is narrow and current code exposes tile geometry, selection, and commit functions that can support a concrete design without more reporter evidence.
evidence: The reporter asks for mouse selection analogous to Alt+Tab instead of hotkey-only cycling.
AltWindowCycle computes tile rectangles and maintains a selected index.
The overlay WndProc handles timers and settings changes but no mouse move or button messages.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a full interaction design for pointer hit-testing, hover selection, click commit, cancellation, focus, accessibility, pagination, and keyboard parity.

issue_context.summary: Window Hopper already renders selectable tiles but its native overlay handles no mouse activation messages, making pointer selection a bounded interaction design.
known_information: Window Hopper displays a native overlay of same-application windows.
TileRect and selection state already define visible hit targets.
Current activation commits the selected window through ForceForeground.
inferences: Mouse support can likely be implemented within the existing overlay by hit-testing visible tile rectangles and reusing SetSelection and Commit.
issue_context.analysis: The previous artifact exposed a premature approve_design action despite having no completed design. The correct fresh state is actionable design_in_progress with no approval button until pointer lifetime and accessibility details converge.
initial_investigation: src/modules/AltWindowCycle/AltWindowCycle.cpp contains TileRect, SetSelection, Commit, and the overlay WndProc.
Repository search found no WM_MOUSE, WM_LBUTTON, or pointer handling in the current overlay.
AltWindowCycle.UnitTests already cover layout geometry and selection wrapping.
